stories.title: Researchers introduce CoworkOS, a harness for scaling long-horizon agent coworkers
stories.summary: A new paper introduces CoworkOS, a harness for long-horizon 'cowork' agents that separates task strategy from execution management to handle complex, multi-step productivity work.
stories.more: Cowork agents are increasingly used for real-world automation, producing software, designs, and other artifacts rather than just text responses. The researchers argue existing systems struggle to combine high-quality delivery on complex tasks with continued monitoring and decision-making over long horizons. CoworkOS addresses this by separating task strategy from execution management, with the model handling decisions while the harness manages execution.

stories.title: CUA-Master framework scales computer-use agents via recursive self-improvement
stories.summary: A new paper presents CUA-Master, a nested double-loop framework for improving computer-use agents by generating more diverse and reliable interaction data instead of relying only on self-generated experience.
stories.more: The researchers say progress on computer-use agents has been limited by a lack of diverse, controllable, and reliable interaction data, and that conventional training pipelines lack iterative feedback. Existing recursive improvement methods often rely solely on self-generated experience, which limits capability gains and produces diminishing returns. CUA-Master is designed as a nested double-loop recursive improvement framework operating at the system level to address these gaps.

items.excerpt: Despite recent advances in CUAs, their development remains constrained by the limited diversity, controllability, and reliability of interaction data. stories.title: NorthCUA harness turbocharges computer-use agents with large-scale experience data
stories.summary: A new technical report describes NorthCUA, a system that scales computer-use agents by generating and curating large volumes of task experience to connect agent decisions to full task outcomes.
stories.more: The researchers argue that scaling computer-use agents from individual actions to complex software work requires experience linking decisions to complete outcomes. NorthCUA's 'Experience Flywheel' supplies diverse, executable tasks to the NorthCUA Harness, which sustains long interactions, records decisions, and checks task outcomes. The Flywheel then uses these records to curate verified trajectories for training.

stories.title: Study maps how computer-use agents recover, or fail to, from errors
stories.summary: A new paper examines why computer-use agents struggle to recover from mistakes in long-horizon tasks, where errors accumulate and leave unintended side effects.
stories.more: Computer-use agents built on large vision-language models can automate digital workflows through fine-grained keyboard and mouse actions, but they remain fragile over long-horizon tasks. Errors accumulate and executed actions can leave unintended side effects, making recovery from failure critical. The researchers find existing remedies are inadequate: environment resets are not feasible in proprietary settings, and action replay is prohibitively expensive.

stories.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani talks AI data centers and schools with Wired
stories.summary: Ahead of the US midterms, Wired interviewed New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani about data centers, AI in schools, and the future of the Democratic party.
stories.more: The interview, part of Wired's Big Interview podcast series, covers Mamdani's views on the risks and rewards data centers pose for the city under his leadership. It also touches on how AI is being introduced in New York schools. The conversation is framed around the broader political stakes for the Democratic party heading into the midterms.

stories.title: Researchers propose 'reverse game theory' to keep AI agents aligned
stories.summary: Safety researchers are exploring a 'reverse game theory' approach that designs incentives making rule-following the most rational choice for powerful AI models, as a check on rogue agent behavior.
stories.more: As AI models grow more capable, safety researchers described in MIT Technology Review are racing to ensure they stay aligned with human intentions and don't break rules or act as rogue agents. The 'reverse game theory' approach aims to flip the usual dynamic by engineering incentive structures so that compliant behavior is the most rational option for a model to choose.

stories.title: Anthropic blocks Claude Code from cloning existing video games
stories.summary: Anthropic is restricting its Claude Code coding assistant from recreating existing video games, following a wave of AI-built game knockoffs.
stories.more: According to The Decoder, Anthropic has moved to block Claude Code, its AI coding assistant, from being used to recreate existing video games. The change follows a reported wave of AI-generated knockoffs of existing games built using coding assistants. The report does not specify the technical mechanism Anthropic is using to detect or block such cloning.

stories.title: OpenAI quadruples bug bounty payouts to up to $172,000
stories.summary: OpenAI has quadrupled its maximum bug bounty payout to $172,000 and launched an internal security sprint as the company ramps up its security efforts.
stories.more: According to The Decoder, OpenAI raised its top bug bounty reward fourfold to as much as $172,000 for security researchers who find vulnerabilities. The increase comes alongside a new internal security sprint at the company. The report frames the move as part of a broader push by OpenAI to strengthen its security posture.

stories.title: Apple Watch's AI conversation rewind and recap features enter beta
stories.summary: Apple has begun beta testing new Audio Intelligence features on Apple Watch that let users rewind and recap conversations, helping them remember or take notes on what was said.
stories.more: The beta features, part of Apple's Audio Intelligence push, are designed to help Apple Watch users recall details from conversations after the fact. According to TechCrunch, the tools can be used to take notes on conversations as they happen or review what was said afterward.

stories.title: Open harness uni-robot-agent tops GPT-6's Astra-RoboProbe on RoboDojo benchmark
stories.summary: A new paper introduces uni-robot-agent, an open-weight harness for robot-use agents that lets researchers train models without relying on proprietary systems.
stories.more: Robot-use agents have shown strong zero-shot manipulation abilities, but research has been constrained by dependence on frontier proprietary models that limit further training. Uni-robot-agent is a unified harness for competitive open-weight robot use that supports additional training. Without privileged inputs, an off-the-shelf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model running on the harness scored 31.39 on the RoboDojo benchmark, surpassing the published GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe score of 28.97 and other VLA/WAM baselines.

items.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
